meta.descrizione: Taranto, Italy, 2087, Holy Thursday. A 2.5D action platformer with characters that look like stop-motion puppets and a cardboard city where air and arms are paid for in instalments. In development; a personal project.
meta.og_descrizione: Taranto, 2087. It's Holy Thursday, and they've come to repossess his arm.
meta.og_alt: GIG, a puppet with a white beard and a yellow shirt, walks along the cemetery wall, covered in torn posters.

eroe.motto_2: The hooded penitents set out from the Carmine church, barefoot.
eroe.motto_3: At the cemetery, two Esattori come to repossess an arm.
eroe.alt: GIG, a puppet with a white beard and a yellow shirt, walks along the cemetery's tufa wall, covered in torn posters, next to an iron gate.
eroe.didascalia: The side gate of the cemetery, on the prologue set. In-game capture, November 2026.

gioco.attacco: You run, double-jump and clamber over a city made of cardboard. The camera follows GIG from the side like an operator on a film set: it closes in when the Esattori arrive, cranes up when the view opens out, and turns with the street.
gioco.alt: The cemetery seen from the side, in game: GIG runs across paving red with dust, past a row of headstones and crosses, with the chapels behind.
gioco.didascalia: The cemetery, in game. GIG moves in staccato, 15 poses a second, like a puppet.
gioco.platform_testo: Tombs, rooftops, scaffolding, air purifiers. Anything that will hold a fifty-year-old man is a platform.
gioco.arene_testo: The Esattori, SIDERA's repo men, are people from the neighbourhood, hired by the day, with an arm on lease. You don't take them down: you take them off the leash.
gioco.hacking_testo: The cyber arm opens what SIDERA has locked. Every one of its functions used to be a paid extra: GIG takes them back, one at a time.

mondo.p1: At San Brunone cemetery the white headstones don't stay white: anyone from the Tamburi district has always known that. By 2087 the steelworks has been cold for more than sixty years, sealed under white domes. The red cloud is still there. SIDERA calls it “clean-up steam”.
mondo.p2: For generations Taranto had to choose between work and health. SIDERA found the answer: it rents out both. The air is called ARIA+ (aria means air). The arm, for those hurt on the job, is called MANODOPERA (“workforce”). Miss a payment and it's switched off remotely. Then the Esattori come.
mondo.chiusa: By 2087 almost everything in Taranto has changed. Not the rites of Holy Week. And someone still writes on the walls.
mondo.manifesto_label: A SIDERA advert, from the world of the game
mondo.manifesto_nota: A made-up ad, like SIDERA itself.
mondo.torretta_alt: A smooth white and mint-green plastic ARIA+ tower. Someone has stencilled on it in black spray paint: CHI RESPIRA PAGA. GIG stands next to it, seen from behind.
mondo.torretta_didascalia: An ARIA+ tower, in the workshop. The writing isn't SIDERA's: “if you breathe, you pay”.

gig.alt: GIG in close-up, in profile, in front of a tufa wall covered in posters: an eye, a hand, a sun, a wave.
gig.p1: A conveyor belt on the Linea took his left arm. He built the new one himself, in his mother's garage, and then built one for half the city. When Mimmo, his childhood friend, died, he asked too many questions: within a week SIDERA had taken his job and his house, and struck his name off the patents. And switched off his arm.
gig.p2: Gruff, wry and stubborn. He can fix anything except his own life.
gig.nota: He won't get there alone. You'll meet the others along the way.

lab.vuoto: Nothing yet: the set is still being built.

come.v1: It's a video game, made in Unreal Engine 5. It isn't hand-shot stop motion: the characters are 3D models that imitate puppets, and move with the same staccato as real puppets.
come.v2: The set imitates a diorama of cardboard, modelling clay and salvaged bits, as if Taranto had been built by a kid: young hands, but skilled ones. What belongs to the people is handmade. SIDERA's things are moulded plastic: smooth, not a fingerprint on them.
come.v3: Some of the tools are AI: reference images and painted surfaces with ChatGPT, 3D models with Meshy, voices with HeyGen, music with Suno.
come.v4: It's a personal project. It isn't for sale and has no release date.

piede.fantasia: Ctrl-Alt-Revenge is a work of fiction. SIDERA, ARIA+, MANODOPERA and all the characters are made up, and any resemblance to real people or companies is coincidental. The places and rituals of Taranto are real, and we treat them with respect.
piede.caratteri: Fonts: Bungee, Archivo (SIL Open Font License), Permanent Marker, Special Elite (Apache 2.0). The cardboard surfaces come from the game's set.

demo.attacco: The prologue is already playable: the cemetery and the gate. This is a work-in-progress demo from 18 November 2026, not the finished game.
demo.alt: The cemetery seen from the side, from the game: GIG runs along the red dusty paving in front of a row of gravestones and crosses, with the chapels in the background.
demo.d1: The levels are still grey boxes. The cardboard set is on its way. The characters, though, are already the puppets.
demo.d2: There are no cutscenes yet, and the electric water is harmless, for now.
demo.d3: 64-bit Windows. Best with a gamepad: the controls are in the README file inside the zip.
demo.d4: Windows may warn that the program is not recognised: it is an unsigned executable.
demo.d5: It is not for sale and has no release date.
demo.nota: The file is in the project's GitHub releases, as a pre-release.
